title: Internationalization in React
summary: Prepare React interfaces for translated text, regional formats, and different writing directions.

subtopics.title: Separate messages from components
subtopics.explanation: Keep user-facing sentences in message catalogs rather than scattering them through JSX. A message may include named values and plural rules. Libraries such as react-i18next can load catalogs and select the active language. A catalog is like a menu translated for each location.

subtopics.title: Use locale-aware formatting
subtopics.explanation: Use `Intl.NumberFormat`, `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, and related browser APIs to format values. The same date or price can appear differently by region. Store a clear underlying value, then format it for display. A timestamp is the recipe; the locale chooses the clock face.

subtopics.title: Handle grammar and plural rules
subtopics.explanation: Languages do not all form plurals the same way. A message should express a count using locale rules rather than appending an “s” in code. Translation catalogs can represent singular, plural, and other language-specific forms. A sentence template needs to fit the language, not just the number.

subtopics.title: Support direction and flexible layout
subtopics.explanation: Some languages read right to left, and translated text may be much longer than the original. Use logical CSS properties and test menus, forms, and dialogs in both directions. Avoid fixed widths that cut off text. A flexible sign must still fit when its words change.

subtopics.title: Plan loading and fallback
subtopics.explanation: Choose what language to show before translations load, and provide a safe fallback when a message is missing. Avoid a page that flashes one language and then another. Test a complete user task after switching locale, including errors and confirmation messages.

foundations.overview: Internationalization prepares an interface for different languages and regions. Text length, plural rules, dates, currencies, and writing direction can all change. A library such as react-i18next helps organize messages and select a language. The interface still needs room for longer translations and right-to-left layouts.
foundations.mentalModel: A locale is a set of instructions for how words, numbers, dates, and direction should appear to a particular audience.
foundations.whyItMatters: Hard-coded wording and date formats can exclude users and make a product costly to expand to new regions.
foundations.formalDefinition: Internationalization is the design of software so that language and locale-specific content can be adapted without rewriting application behavior.
foundations.browserPerspective: The browser provides Intl formatters for dates, numbers, and currencies; translation libraries manage message catalogs and language selection.
foundations.realWorldUsage: Keep translated messages in catalogs, format values with Intl, and test the layout using long and right-to-left text.
foundations.businessImpact: Localization helps a product serve users in different languages and markets.
foundations.engineeringImpact: Message keys and locale rules need ownership, fallback behavior, and translation review.
foundations.performanceImpact: Load only the language resources needed for the current experience when catalogs grow large.
commonMisconceptions: Dates, numbers, plural rules, layout, and direction also vary.
Word order and grammar differ; translate complete messages with variables.
A locale only identifies a language
It can also specify regional formatting and conventions.

keyTakeaways: Keep user-facing sentences in message catalogs rather than scattering them through JSX.
Languages do not all form plurals the same way.

codeLab.title: Switch translated messages
codeLab.instructions: Create a small language switcher that displays the same greeting in English or Spanish. Keep text in a message map rather than inside conditional markup.
codeLab.expectedOutput: Changing the select control updates the greeting.
hints: Break the task into state, event handling, and rendered feedback.
Keep the interface accessible with labels and meaningful button text.
